title: Claimant Identity Verification Reuse Periods and Post-Failure Pathway Change Terms
content:
A completed Claimant Identity Verification remains usable for a later claim of the same claimant for a reuse period that depends on the pathway that produced it. The schedule also states, per pathway, the re-verification window after a profile change and whether a failed case may move to another pathway.

| Pathway that produced the verification (or on which the case failed) | Reuse period after the verified date (calendar months) | Re-verification window after a change of bank account or mailing address (calendar days) | Failed case may be moved to another pathway |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | 18 | 30 | yes |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | 18 | 30 | yes |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | 24 | 30 | yes |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | 24 | 30 | yes |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | 12 | 30 | yes |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | 24 | 30 | no |

### Footnotes

1. The reuse period is the number of calendar months after the verified date during which a completed verification is reused for a later claim of the same claimant.
2. The re-verification window is the number of calendar days after a change of bank account or mailing address within which a later claim needs a new verification even though a reusable one exists.
3. The final column states whether the claimant may move a failed case to another pathway; Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification is the only pathway on which a failed case may not move.
4. Reuse periods are longest (24 months) for verifications produced in person at an American Job Center or USPS retail office or on identity theft re-verification, 18 months for online and video proofing, and shortest (12 months) for documentary verification by mail.
